← DREW’S MUSIC ENGINEOperating guide · v1

COMPOSE ONCE. RENDER WHEN NEEDED.

The studio’s operating guide.

A small, reusable instrument for turning complete compositions into finished audio.

The workflow

  1. Open the studio and wait for Sound collection ready.
  2. Load a JSON composition or a standard MIDI file. A full example is already loaded on the first visit.
  3. Choose dry, room, or hall reverb. Set its amount and sample rate if needed.
  4. Choose Render music. Rendering runs in a separate worker, without recording live playback.
  5. Listen and download the WAV or MP3. Keep the JSON or MIDI file to revise the arrangement later.

The bank is GeneralUser GS 1.471. Stereo WAV uses 16-bit PCM; MP3 uses 192 kbps. Renders include a 2-second release tail, or 4 seconds for hall reverb. Rendered audio is kept in this tab until it is replaced or closed. Download to keep it. The last JSON composition is recovered on this browser when storage is available; MIDI and finished audio are not recovered.

Composition format

GM programs are numbered 1–128. Note values can be MIDI numbers 0–127 or names such as C4, F#3, and Bb4. C4 is middle C (60). All note positions and durations are in quarter-note beats, including compound meters. Velocity is 1–127. Every instrument part gets its own channel; percussion uses channel 9, which is MIDI channel 10.

{
  "format": "drews-music-engine",
  "version": 1,
  "title": "A Small Beginning",
  "tempo": 96,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "name": "Marimba",
      "program": 13,
      "volume": 0.8,
      "pan": -0.15,
      "reverbSend": 0.55,
      "notes": [
        {"note": "C5", "beat": 0, "duration": 0.75, "velocity": 74},
        {"note": "E5", "beat": 1, "duration": 0.75, "velocity": 82},
        {"note": "G5", "beat": 2, "duration": 1.5, "velocity": 70}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Optional song fields: description, durationSeconds (adds silence after the last note), and tempoChanges: [{"beat": 8, "bpm": 110}]. Optional track fields: channel (0–15), drums: true, controls: [{"beat": 0, "controller": 64, "value": 127}, {"beat": 4, "controller": 64, "value": 0}], and pitchBends: [{"beat": 2, "value": 8192}]. Pitch bend uses the current MIDI bend range; 8192 is center. Part volume is 0–1 and pan is −1 (left) to +1 (right).

Limits: 16 parts, unique channels, 30,000 JSON notes, five minutes of music, and 8 MB per uploaded song. The MIDI loader supports format 0 or 1, a single MIDI port, tempo maps and channel messages. Device-specific SysEx is ignored. Use GM instrument assignments for portable results.

For browser agents

When the browser exposes WebMCP, the open page registers these actions. Discover the actual tools before invoking them. If WebMCP is unavailable, use the visible composition textarea or file loader and the render/download controls.

ActionPurpose
music_engine_statusRead SoundFont readiness, composition, progress, errors and output.
load_compositionSupply {"composition": {…}} to load a complete song.
set_audio_optionsSet reverb, reverbAmount (0–0.7), sampleRate (44100 or 48000), and normalize.
start_audio_renderStart a render and return immediately. Read status until busy is false.
list_gm_instrumentsRead actual program names and numbers from the sound bank.

After rendering, check lastError is null and output.stale is false. Start the browser’s download listener before clicking Download WAV or Download MP3. Retrieve the downloaded file and share it with Drew. Keep an editable composition when it will be useful later.

Piano: 1 · Music box: 11 · Vibraphone: 12 · Marimba: 13 · Xylophone: 14 · Nylon guitar: 25 · Acoustic bass: 33 · Strings: 49 · Harp: 47 · Flute: 74. Download the full instrument catalog.
